expectations.text: Identifies SAQ A for card-not-present merchants with all cardholder data functions fully outsourced to PCI-compliant third parties (redirect or compliant iframe)
expectations.evidence: "you are most likely eligible for SAQ A"; "fully outsourced all cardholder data functions... to PCI DSS validated third-party service provider(s)" (redirect or provider-hosted iframe)

expectations.text: States the merchant's site must not receive/transmit/store cardholder data — only pointing to the payment processor
expectations.evidence: "no cardholder data touches merchant infrastructure at all, not even in logs or memory"

expectations.text: Notes SAQ A now includes requirements addressing e-commerce skimming risk (script management 6.4.3 and change/tamper detection 11.6.1 style controls)
expectations.evidence: "Requirement 6.4.3... Requirement 11.6.1... These two apply even to SAQ A merchants" targeting Magecart-style skimming

expectations.text: Distinguishes SAQ A-EP: merchants whose site affects the security of the payment redirect (e.g., JavaScript-created payment form) face the much larger SAQ A-EP
expectations.evidence: "you likely fall into SAQ A-EP instead, which has significantly more requirements (roughly 40+)... because your web server is considered to influence the security of the payment process"

expectations.text: Advises confirming SAQ eligibility with the acquirer, which determines validation requirements
expectations.evidence: "walk through the current SAQ A and A-EP eligibility criteria... with your team (and ideally your acquirer or a QSA)"
